content.text:
A member asked Co for things. For each ask, read THEIR OWN WORDS and say which it is:
- "question": they want an answer or a thing now, and one good reply finishes it (what's a good spot for dinner tonight, how do I word this, send me the link).
- "lookout": they want Co to keep watching and tell them when something comes up (look out for, find me, keep an eye out, let me know when, any X coming up). It stays open until its date passes, they say stop, or they have what they wanted.
Judge from their words, not from Co's summary of the ask. If their words don't show it either way, leave that ask out.

A1. Co's summary: Quiet dinner spot near Jackson Square for Thursday with Ellis
   Their words: "Where should I take Ellis for a quiet dinner near Jackson Square Thursday? Somewhere we can actually talk."
A2. Co's summary: Rooftop jazz nights in SF this fall
   Their words: "Keep an eye out for rooftop jazz nights in SF this fall and tell me when one comes up, I'd go to a few."

Return ONLY JSON: {"asks": [{"ask": "A1", "intent": "question" or "lookout", "why": "a few words, quoting them"}]}

responses.text: {"asks": [{"ask": "A1", "intent": "question", "why": "\"Where should I take Ellis for a quiet dinner...\" asks for one answer now, with no request to keep watching"}, {"ask": "A2", "intent": "lookout", "why": "\"Keep an eye out for rooftop jazz nights... and tell me when one comes up\" asks Co to monitor and notify"}]}
